observations:
LM2 Torah #6 is a self-contained, five-sentence teaching. It introduces exactly two conceptual domains — the domain of joy/holy sweat (Package 1) and the domain of sadness/turbid blood (Package 2) — which are each other's polar opposites. There are no additional independent domains with 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language that would constitute a separate package beyond these two.

The Torah's conceptual structure is deliberately minimal and tight:

1. GOOD DOMAIN (Package 1): שמחה — זיעה טובה — שמחת יום טוב — יום טוב — דמים זכים — זה היום עשה ה'. All six nodes are interconnected expressions of holy joy and physiological purity.

2. EVIL/NEGATIVE DOMAIN (Package 2): עצבות — טחול — עכירות הדמים — ארס. All four nodes are expressions of spiritual sadness and physiological impurity/toxicity.

3. MEDIATING MECHANISM: זיעה (sweat in general, including the specific holy sweat of Package 1) functions as the eitza bridge — it is the action that destroys Package 2 and produces Package 1. Sweat itself is not a third domain; it belongs to Package 1 as the instrument of the holy.

Candidate for a third package was considered: Could 'חולשות' (weakness/illness) constitute its own package? No — it appears only once as an effect of excessive turbid blood ('עַל-יְדֵי-זֶה בָּאִין חֻלְשׁוֹת') and is an eitza consequence of Package 2, not a bechina-connected conceptual domain in its own right. It has no bechina partners in the text and belongs within the negative/illness domain of Package 2 as an eitza output.

Candidate for a third package: Could the sick person's experience (חולה — the sick person who sweats and receives joy) form a package? No — the sick person is introduced only as an observational example in the final sentence ('וְזֶה שֶׁאָנוּ רוֹאִין, שֶׁהַחוֹלֶה תֵּכֶף כְּשֶׁמַּזִּיעַ נִמְשָׁךְ עָלָיו שִׂמְחָה'). It is an illustration, not an independent conceptual domain.

Conclusion: The two packages identified — שִׂמְחָה וְזֵעָה טוֹבָה (good/positive) and עַצְבוּת וְטֻמְאַת הַדָּם (evil/negative) — fully exhaust the conceptual structure of this Torah. They form a perfect good/evil mirror: one domain of holy overflow that produces joy, and one domain of impure accumulation that produces sadness. The sweat is the eitza that moves from evil to good.
